title: Basic operations and coefficient reduction
statement:
For the derived-complete
coefficient categories, reduction $\mathcal O_E\to A_{E,n}$ commutes
with derived pullback, tensor, ordinary direct image and compact-support
direct image on their stated bounded domains. Finite reduction
$A_{E,n}\to A_{E,m}$ commutes with pullback, tensor and
compact-support direct image on the finite-Tor domains.
For $\mathcal O_E\to A_{E,n}$, internal Hom and evaluation commute
with reduction for arbitrary first variables on the stated integral
domains. Between finite quotient rings, the elementary comparison
proved here assumes that the first variable is
site-perfect; this includes
the coefficient dual of a perfect complex at a point.
For admissible
exceptional adjoints, use the coefficient comparisons required in
that admissibility hypothesis. The same operations and comparisons
commute with rationalization
and common-stage
scalar extension. All the displayed comparisons preserve the tensor
associativity maps, evaluations, units and counits used to construct
the projection and exchange transformations.

proof.text: Integral pullback and completed tensor constructibility with their finite reduction isomorphisms are integralOperations_preserve_constructible; the integral direct-image clause is the first two parts of sfIntegralDirectImage_constructible; finite-level compact-support reduction is the third part of finiteCompactSupportConstructibility (finite-Tor constructibility contains intrinsic constructibility); integral internal-Hom reduction is integralHomReduction; the integral scalar comparisons are integralOperationsScalarExtension, whose stalk hypothesis follows from invertibility of l in each residue field because the residue map of a local ring is local. The finite pullback/tensor and quotient maps are isomorphisms by construction, and their quotient condition is a projection of derivedPullbackTensorIso. Apply basicOperationReductionAndEvaluation for integral compact-support reduction and finite, site-perfect and scalar Hom evaluation; apply basicOperationCoefficientCoherence for the completed coefficient actions and mate equations. Read the rational and common-stage representative laws from the existing unique specifications. Project the integral, rational, and common-stage pullback associativity, unit, scalar, and reduction laws from derivedPullbackTensorIso. Assemble the conjunction. The final exceptional-adjoint assertion is precisely its explicit admissibility hypothesis.

blueprint_update.statement:
For the condensed integral categories $\Dbc(-,\mathcal O_E)$, whose objects
are derived $\pi_E$-complete $\mathcal O_{E,X}$-complexes
([def-pe-derived-complete], [sk-prop-integral-criterion]), reduction
$\mathcal O_E\to A_{E,n}$, $K\mapsto K_n=K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_{E,X}}(A_{E,n})_X$,
commutes with derived pullback, tensor, ordinary direct image and
compact-support direct image on their stated bounded domains. Finite
reduction $A_{E,n}\to A_{E,m}$ commutes with pullback, tensor and
compact-support direct image on the finite-Tor domains.
For $\mathcal O_E\to A_{E,n}$, internal Hom and evaluation commute
with reduction for arbitrary first variables on the stated integral
domains. Between finite quotient rings, the elementary comparison
proved here assumes that the first variable is
site-perfect; this includes
the coefficient dual of a perfect complex at a point.
For admissible exceptional adjoints at the finite levels, use the
coefficient comparisons required in that admissibility hypothesis; at
$\mathcal O_E$ the comparison for $Rf^!$ is that of [sk-prop-scalar-six].
The same operations and comparisons commute with localization
$\mathcal O_E\to E$ and with extension of scalars $E\to F\to\Qlb$ on the
condensed categories ([sk-def-sfb-coefficient-comparisons],
[sk-prop-scalar-six]). All the displayed comparisons preserve the tensor
associativity maps, evaluations, units and counits used to construct
the projection and exchange transformations.

*Formalisation status (the statement is unchanged).* One clause is not yet
formalised: in the pro-étale model, that reduction modulo $\mathfrak m_E$
(that is, $\mathcal O_E\to A_{E,n}$) carries the projection map
$\mathrm{PF}_{f,K,L}$ to the projection map of the reductions
$\mathrm{PF}_{f,K_n,L_n}$. The étale projection map and the pro-étale
compact-support exchange map are covered, but the pro-étale projection map
needs that the pro-étale pullback preserves flat objects for a general
coefficient ring, which is not yet available. The completed pro-étale
projection formula for the scalar extensions $\mathcal O_E\to\mathcal O_{E'}$
depends on this clause (or on a comparison of the pullback from the étale to
the pro-étale site with derived completion), and is formalised so far only for
pro-étale realizations $K=\nu^*K_0$, $L=\nu^*L_0$ of étale complexes and
under the additional hypothesis that both sides of the étale projection map
$Rf_!K_0\otimes^{\mathbf L}L_0\to Rf_!(K_0\otimes^{\mathbf L}Lf^*L_0)$ are derived
complete.

proof.text:
Pullback and tensor are computed with K-flat resolutions in
[def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]; reassociation of the same
threefold tensor product proves their reduction comparisons and
the corresponding associativity identities. If the first argument
of internal Hom is site-perfect in [def-weil-site-perfect-complex],
choose a bounded finite-projective representative locally. Its
termwise Hom commutes with coefficient change. This identifies the
actual evaluation maps, since evaluation of a finite-projective
module is compatible with tensoring the coefficients.

The two-term free resolution
$[\mathcal O_E\xrightarrow{\pi_E^n}\mathcal O_E]$
shows that $A_{E,n}$ is perfect over $\mathcal O_E$ ([lem-weil-pbc-standard-quotients-perfect]).
For internal Hom this gives, without a perfectness assumption on $K$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_E}(K,L)\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n}
&\cong R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_E}
(K,L\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n})\\
&\cong R\mathcal Hom_{A_{E,n}}(K_n,L_n).
\end{aligned}
$$

The first map commutes Hom in its second variable with the finite
two-term cone. The second is extension–restriction of scalars
adjunction. Both are the maps adjoint to tensoring evaluation, so this
is the specified coefficient comparison, compatible with evaluation.
Consequently [lemma-weil-pbc-perfect-projection-formula] gives
$(Rf_*K)_n\simeq Rf_*K_n$; no completion intervenes, since the objects of
$\Dbc(-,\mathcal O_E)$ are already derived complete
([sk-prop-integral-criterion]), and this is the reduction comparison of
[sk-prop-scalar-six]. Applying this to the
proper factor and using extension by zero gives the compact-support
comparison, which is [det-prop-scalar-six-compact-support] for the map
$\mathcal O_E\to A_{E,n}$.
Between finite levels use
[lem-fix-compact-support-coefficient-change]. The corresponding
comparison for an exceptional right adjoint is precisely the
coefficient compatibility in
[def-weil-exceptional-adjoint-admissibility]; it is invoked only
under that explicit hypothesis.

At the field coefficients, the comparisons along $\mathcal O_E\to E$ and
$E\to F\to\Qlb$ are the coefficient comparisons of
[sk-def-sfb-coefficient-comparisons]; by [sk-prop-scalar-six] they are
isomorphisms on the condensed categories $\Dctf=\Dbc$ and respect
composition, units, counits and evaluation maps. Each asserted identity is
an identity between composites of the tensor associativity map, the
evaluation or the adjunction maps already described, so it holds at the
field coefficients as well. This proves compatibility of the specified maps,
beyond the existence of comparison isomorphisms.
